transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-25
Time: 09:00 AM PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (CTO - Helix), Sara Gomez (Infra), David Park (Product), Leila Torres (Security)

Summary (auto): Helix is doing a quick evaluation of Redwood for an internal pilot. Primary asks: fast onboarding for devs (time-to-first-token), trial credits, security/compliance docs, and a follow-up benchmark to validate latency and cost.

00:00 Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, super quick intro from our side. I'm Jordan, AE, and with me is Priya our SE.
00:07 Marcus Li: Thanks. Marcus here, CTO at Helix. We do threat intel and some LLM-assisted triage. Quick background: we have an ML team who prototyped locally but we want something we can roll out to product.
00:18 Jordan Kim: Great, so high level we'll cover the PLG quickstart - free credits, how fast you can get to first token, and options if you need dedicated or private later.
00:28 Priya Patel: Hi all - I'll jump into the technical bits. Curious about current infra - Marcus, are you doing anything self-hosted today for inference?
00:36 Marcus Li: Right now it's a mix, mostly on-prem experiments and some batch jobs on GCP. We don't have a production inference endpoint. A key ask is compliance - SOC2 + KMS and VPC controls.
00:48 Sara Gomez: Also latency: for the triage flow we want sub-200ms tail latency for single-turn prompts if possible, but we know that's hard with larger contexts.
00:58 Priya Patel: Understood. Quick note on time-to-first-token: with Redwood's hosted API you can sign up, get free credits, and call the REST/SDK in under 10 minutes - typical dev path is quickstart repo, API key, then a sample request.
01:12 Jordan Kim: Yep, PLG is designed for that. We usually give initial trial credits and a quickstart link. For teams that need more predictability we have Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem).
01:25 David Park: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private?
01:28 Priya Patel: Sure - Dedicated is still hosted by Redwood but it's reserved capacity for you, with predictable throughput and isolation. Private is for when you need the control plane in your VPC or on-prem package - that's typical for regulated workflows. Both support the same API surface.
01:43 Leila Torres: From security perspective we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration. Also data residency concerns. How much of that is available in the PLG hosted tier?
01:54 Priya Patel: For self-serve/hosted, we provide SOC2 controls, audit logs, and encryption at rest. KMS/HSM for Private and some Dedicated options - we can discuss integration patterns. SAML SSO and enterprise RBAC is usually part of our enterprise plan but we can enable SSO for pilots in some cases.
02:10 Marcus Li: What's the expected onboarding friction? We have a small dev team - do we need infra changes?
02:16 Jordan Kim: Minimal for the quickstart: sign-up, API key, add it to your SDK or curl, then call. If you want Private, there's more work for networking and KMS. But for a 2-4 week pilot we recommend hosted PLG to validate product-market fit.
02:30 Marcus Li: Cool. Cost side - what's the unit pricing and how does batching/kv cache help?
02:36 Priya Patel: Pricing varies by model and tokens. We have Optimize recommendations - batching and KV/prefix caching can reduce per-token costs by reducing repeated computation. For interactive triage you can cache common prefixes and reduce latencies with streaming.
02:49 Sara Gomez: There's also the question of long context windows - our triage logs can be big. Any guidance on quantization or model recommendations?
02:56 Priya Patel: We onboarded numerous open models with different performance profiles. For large contexts we might recommend a quantized model or a sequence partition strategy. We can run a quick benchmark to recommend specific model/quantization combos for your workload.
03:10 David Park: Are there any gotchas with the SDK? We like Node and Python.
03:15 Jordan Kim: We have official SDKs for both and sample apps. The quickstart repo includes a Node example for first token in <10 lines.
03:22 Marcus Li: Ok, security - can we get SOC2 and the network diagram?
03:26 Priya Patel: Yes. I'll send the SOC2 summary and our KMS integration doc after. We also have an architecture diagram for Private deployments.
03:33 Leila Torres: We might need an NDA before sharing some internal prompts, but for the pilot we can share sanitized examples.
03:40 Jordan Kim: That's fine - we can sign an NDA. For benchmarks, do you have a target QPS or concurrency?
03:46 Marcus Li: Peak is small for now - like 10-20 QPS but we care about p95 latency. If things look good we'll scale.
03:54 Priya Patel: 10-20 QPS is straightforward for hosted, may want Dedicated if you need guaranteed SLOs for bursty traffic.
04:02 Jordan Kim: Also routing policies - you can route by latency or cost, and fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
04:09 Sara Gomez: Any mention of competitor tradeoffs? We evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic - our infra folks prefer predictable performance and lower egress costs.
04:19 Jordan Kim: Understood. For cost predictability Dedicated is the usual path - and our Optimize toolkit helps balance latency vs cost.

--- Transcript (detailed) ---
04:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Alright let me share my screen briefly - quickstart repo link in chat: https://redwood.ai/quickstart (link)
04:36 Speaker 2 (Priya): I'll paste our SOC2 summary and KMS doc after the call, and the architecture diagram for Private: docs.redwood.ai/private-arch (link)
04:44 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Thanks. So for the pilot, ideal outcome is we spin up a dev team, validate the triage flow in a week or two, and measure p95 latencies and cost per request.
04:56 Speaker 1 (Jordan): That sounds right. Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks, we give trial credits to cover baseline usage. Our API key flow gives you immediate tokens for dev testing.
05:07 Speaker 3 (Marcus): What's the SLA on hosted?
05:10 Speaker 2 (Priya): Hosted has best-effort for PLG; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime/latency. For serious SLAs and support we discuss reserved capacity and enterprise SLAs.
05:21 Speaker 4 (Leila): For audited customers we need to ensure audit logs are exportable to our SIEM.
05:26 Speaker 2 (Priya): Yes, audit logs and trace hooks can be exported; we also have tracing and per-route dashboards in Console.
05:35 Speaker 3 (Marcus): If we start PLG and later move to Private, what's migration like?
05:40 Speaker 1 (Jordan): It's designed to be smooth - same API and model versions. Private adds network/KMS setup, but you can pin model versions and rollout policies to avoid regressions.
05:50 Speaker 4 (Leila): Encryption keys - can we use our KMS?
05:53 Speaker 2 (Priya): For Private and some Dedicated options, yes you can bring-your-own KMS/HSM. For hosted PLG we manage encryption keys but we provide details of our key management practices.
06:04 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Any perf numbers for the model you'd recommend for triage?
06:08 Speaker 2 (Priya): We typically recommend a small LLM variant for single-turn triage - should hit sub-200ms on optimized hardware for short contexts. For longer contexts expect higher p95. We'll run a bench to confirm.
06:20 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Ok next steps - Jordan will send pricing + trial credits. Priya will send SOC2 summary and KMS doc. Schedule deep dive for benchmarks.
06:29 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Sounds good. One question - are there any known issues with KV cache eviction or prefix caching when doing short interactive flows?
06:36 Speaker 2 (Priya): Good question - eviction behavior depends on session and sequence length; our runtime supports continuous KV caching but it's workload dependent. We'll include notes in the bench plan.
06:47 Speaker 5 (David): Quick nit - sometimes transcripts say KV-cache as K-V dash cache, the docs have examples though.
06:52 Speaker 2 (Priya): Haha yes our docs try to be clear.
06:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Any other questions?
07:00 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Not right now. We'll expect the docs and pricing.
07:04 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great thanks everyone - recap in chat and I'll follow up with links and credits.
